# pikapik

> pikapik (formerly pika-tools) is a free, open-source (MIT) menu bar app for macOS 14 and newer. It collects small conveniences for the keyboard, mouse, windows and Finder in one place. Everything is off until you turn it on.

It is written in Swift and SwiftUI, has no dependencies apart from the 7-Zip tool bundled for archives and FFmpeg and dav1d bundled for the player, runs on Apple silicon and Intel, and is available in 23 languages. Settings can be exported as a file or synced through iCloud.

## What it does
- Game Mode: while you play, Spotlight, Siri, ⌘Tab and Mission Control don't pop up over the game, ⌘Q and ⌘W don't close it, and the display stays on.
- Keep Awake: stop the Mac from sleeping for a chosen time, with display and lid options.
- Battery: see the charge, time until full or time left, the battery's condition, maximum capacity and cycle count, the power adapter and the watts going in or being used, and tips to make it last. It only shows information and never changes how the Mac charges. Only on a Mac with a battery.
- Keyboard: input language switch, key repeat, Home and End keys.
- Mouse: turn off pointer acceleration, tracking speed, scrolling by lines, scroll direction, side buttons, a mouse button that hides the app in front, middle click with three or four fingers on the trackpad.
- Windows: enlarge with the green button, ⌘Q and ⌘W protection, quit an app when its last window closes.
- Dock: click an app's icon in the Dock to hide the app. Keep the Dock on one display: the Dock no longer moves to another display when the pointer pushes against that display's bottom edge, because pikapik turns the move off with the Dock's own setting; to move the Dock on purpose, make another display the main one (not in the Mac App Store version).
- Finder: new file, smaller copy and conversion, Enter to open, ⌘X to cut, Delete to move to the Trash. Hide desktop icons clears the desktop before a call, a recording or a screenshot without moving the files, and Show hidden files shows what macOS hides, the same as ⇧⌘. in Finder; Finder restarts for a moment to apply it, after any copying or moving finishes. In the Mac App Store version Hide desktop icons opens Desktop & Dock in System Settings, and the Finder page shows the ⇧⌘. keys.
- Archives: right-click an archive to extract it, or any file or folder to make a ZIP, 7Z, TAR.GZ or TAR.XZ, with a password or split into parts. It also opens RAR and other archives that macOS can't, and Space shows what is inside. Not in the Mac App Store version.
- Player: videos that QuickTime can't open, such as MKV, WebM, AVI, WMV and FLV, play in their own window, in a small separate app that has no network access and asks for no permissions. It doesn't change which app opens your videos. Subtitles aren't supported yet. Not in the Mac App Store version.
- Uninstaller: remove an app together with the files it keeps on the Mac, put it all back later, and clean up what removed apps left behind. Everything goes to the Trash, nothing is deleted for good. Not in the Mac App Store version.
- Background Tasks: see everything that starts by itself (apps that open at login, background services, helpers inside apps and leftovers of deleted apps), which app added each one, whether it is running and where its file is. Your own background services turn off and back on without deleting anything; tasks for all users or the whole Mac open Login Items in System Settings. In the Mac App Store version the page only shows the tasks.
- Speed Test: check the internet speed and see what it is good for.
- Ports: see which program listens on which port, with its icon, addresses, file, command, folder and process ID, and free the port: Free Up quits the program politely, then offers Force Quit, and asks each time. macOS services and other users' programs are never quit; for AirPlay Receiver, File Sharing, Screen Sharing and Remote Login it names the switch in System Settings. Not in the Mac App Store version: there macOS doesn't let an app see which program holds a port.
- App Volume: every app that plays sound gets its own volume slider and mute button, so you can lower or mute one app without touching the others. Needs macOS 14.2 or newer and the System Audio Recording permission.
- Monitor Brightness: every monitor that macOS can't adjust gets a brightness slider in Settings, and a Brightness row can be added to the menu bar panel. pikapik changes the monitor's own brightness, like its buttons do, or dims the picture if the monitor doesn't respond (never to black). With the Accessibility permission, the brightness keys adjust the monitor under the pointer. The Mac App Store version only dims the picture.
- Pet: a little friend walks along the bottom of the screen behind the windows. It jumps on Space and over the pointer, and you can pick it up and throw it. You can dress it from a wardrobe of more than 30 things and ready-made looks, which are unlocked by awards earned as you play together. Awards are counted only on this Mac, nothing is sent anywhere, and you can erase them in Settings › Pet.
- Permissions: lists every permission the app uses (Accessibility, Input Monitoring, Fan control, Finder Extensions, iCloud Drive, Full Disk Access, System Audio Recording) with a live status and one button, Allow or Turn Off; tools that need a missing permission look half-grey and open this page when clicked. It also cleans up permissions left by deleted apps.

## Install
- Terminal: `/bin/bash -c "$(curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/dev-pikapik/pika-tools/main/install.sh)"` (installs the latest release only if it is signed by its developer and notarized by Apple)
- Homebrew: `brew install --cask dev-pikapik/pika-tools/pikapik`
- Download: https://github.com/dev-pikapik/pika-tools/releases/latest/download/pikapik.dmg
